answer:
Count all triples whose sum is divisible by \(7\), then subtract those with no entry divisible by \(5\).

Among \(1,\ldots,98\), each residue modulo \(7\) occurs \(14\) times. Treat \(99\) as an extra element. For any fixed choice of which entries equal \(99\), provided at least one entry comes from \(1,\ldots,98\), exactly one seventh of the triples have sum divisible by \(7\). The triple \((99,99,99)\) does not. Thus the total is
\[
T=\frac{99^3-1}{7}=138614.
\]

Now exclude the \(19\) multiples of \(5\). The remaining \(80\) numbers have these residue counts:
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
\text{Residue modulo }7&0&1&2&3&4&5&6\\ \hline
\text{Count}&12&12&12&11&11&11&11
\end{array}
\]
View these as a balanced set of \(77\) numbers, with \(11\) in each residue class, plus three extra numbers with residues \(0,1,2\).

Among triples containing at least one number from the balanced set, exactly one seventh have sum divisible by \(7\), giving
\[
\frac{80^3-3^3}{7}.
\]
Among triples formed entirely from the three extras, only the residue triple \((0,0,0)\) qualifies, since their residue sum lies between \(0\) and \(6\). Therefore the number to subtract is
\[
N=\frac{80^3-27}{7}+1=73140.
\]

Since \(5\mid abc\) precisely when at least one entry is divisible by \(5\), the answer is
\[
\boxed{138614-73140=65474}.
\]
